result.topic_en: Change of variables between (p,q) and (t,T) with dt = a dp + b dq, dT = A dp + B dq, and computation of derivatives of the Jacobian h = aB − bA and of the second mixed derivative of log μ with respect to t and T.
result.transcription:
$dt = a\,dp + b\,dq$ ; $a', b', c'$
$dT = A\,dp + B\,dq$ ; $A', B', C'$
$h\,dp = B\,dt - b\,dT$
$h\,dq = -A\,dt + a\,dT$
$h = aB - bA$
$h\frac{dh}{dT} = -\frac{a'bB}{h} + \frac{b'aB}{h}$ [-$\frac{2abB'}{h}$ + ... A-] $(B\,da$ ; $(a\,dB$
$-abB' + aaC'$
$+bAb' - aAc'$ $\quad -A\,db$
$+bbA' - abB'$ $\quad -b\,dA$
$= bbA' - 2abB' + aaC'$
$- bBa' + (aB+Ab)b' - aAc'$

$\frac{h\,dh}{dT} = bbA' - 2abB' + aaC'$
$-\mu\mathfrak{E}c' + 2\mu\mathfrak{F}b' - \mu\mathfrak{G}a'$
$\frac{d\log\mu}{dt} =$ [-$\frac{B}{h\mu}\frac{d\mu}{dp}$-] $+ \frac{B}{h\mu}\frac{d\mu}{dp} - \frac{A}{h\mu}\cdot\frac{d\mu}{dq}$
$\frac{dd\log\mu}{dt\,dT} = -\left(\frac{B}{\mu}\frac{d\mu}{dp} - \frac{A\,d\mu}{\mu\,dq}\right)\frac{1}{h^3}\left\{\begin{array}{l} bbA' - 2abB' + aaC' \\ -\mu\mathfrak{E}c' + 2\mu\mathfrak{F}b' - \mu\mathfrak{G}a'\end{array}\right\}$
$-\frac{1}{\mu\mu hh}\left\{\frac{B\,d\mu}{dp} - \frac{A\,d\mu}{dq}\right\}\left\{-\frac{b\,d\mu}{dp} + \frac{a\,d\mu}{dq}\right\}$
$+\frac{1}{hh\mu}\left\{-Bb\cdot\frac{dd\mu}{dp^2} + (aB+bA)\frac{dd\mu}{dp\,dq} - aA\frac{dd\mu}{dq^2}\right\}$
$+\frac{1}{hh\mu}\left\{(-bB' + aC')\frac{d\mu}{dp} + (bA' - aB')\frac{d\mu}{dq}\right\}$

methods.what: Inversion of the linear differential relations between (t,T) and (p,q) via the Jacobian h
Derivative of the Jacobian h with respect to T expressed via second derivatives a', b', c', A', B', C'
Derivative of log μ with respect to t via chain rule
Second mixed derivative of log μ with respect to t and T in terms of p,q derivatives
